Per-layer LayerNorm reduces differences in activation scale before aggregation; otherwise larger-norm layers can dominate despite small mixing weights. ELMo provides a static baseline: learned softmax layer weights plus an overall learned scale, with optional normalization before mixing. Sharing affine gain/bias across layers ties their coordinate calibration but still computes each layer’s statistics separately; independent affine parameters permit layer-specific rescaling, confounding interpretation of mixing weights. LayerNorm also changes backward gradients, so gains need not indicate better feature selection. [ELMo](https://aclanthology.org/N18-1202.pdf), [LayerNorm analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.07013).

Intermediate aggregation introduces shorter loss-to-layer gradient paths. Residual-network research establishes the optimization benefits of direct signal propagation; applying that explanation to a particular aggregation module remains a hypothesis requiring controls. Proposed diagnostic: detach intermediate features only at aggregation branches while preserving the backbone’s normal gradient path, then retrain. This preserves forward access to intermediate features while removing their extra gradient routes, although backbone adaptation necessarily changes. [Identity Mappings](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.05027).

Recommended ablations within one jointly trained NextItNet: final-layer baseline; final-layer plus identical output normalization; uniform intermediate averaging; static learned softmax weights; input-dependent gating. Cross aggregation variants with no normalization, non-affine per-layer LayerNorm, shared affine parameters, and independent affine parameters; keep output normalization and overall scale identical. Add a final-layer-only MLP/projection with comparable trainable parameters and compute. Retrain each control under identical seeds, sampling, optimizer, updates, and validation protocol. Measure feature norms, layerwise gradient norms, gate variability, and convergence alongside macro validation HR@10. Dynamic gating should outperform normalized static weights and matched final-layer capacity before attributing gains to input-dependent layer selection.
